result.builder:
Make one pull request that meets every line below:
- math.js exports clamp(x, lo, hi), which returns x limited to the range lo to hi
- clamp(x, lo, hi) throws a RangeError when lo is greater than hi
- README.md documents every function math.js exports
- npm test passes

Current state: math.js is CommonJS and exports { add, subtract, multiply } via module.exports. README.md has an '## API' section with '### add(a, b)' and '### multiply(a, b)' entries, but subtract is NOT documented. Tests live in test/math.test.js and run with `npm test` (`node --test`, Node 22).

Steps:
1. In math.js add a function clamp(x, lo, hi) with a short doc comment, in the same style as the existing functions. First, if lo > hi, throw new RangeError with a clear message (for example naming lo and hi). Otherwise return x limited to the range: lo if x < lo, hi if x > hi, else x (for example Math.min(Math.max(x, lo), hi)). lo equal to hi is a valid range and must not throw. Add clamp to module.exports alongside add, subtract, multiply; keep the existing exports unchanged.
2. In README.md, under '## API', add a '### subtract(a, b)' entry (returns `a` minus `b`, with a small example) and a '### clamp(x, lo, hi)' entry that says it returns `x` limited to the range `lo` to `hi`, that it throws a RangeError when `lo` is greater than `hi`, and gives an example such as clamp(140, 0, 100) // 100 and clamp(-5, 0, 100) // 0. Every function math.js exports must have its name followed by '(' written in README.md.
3. In test/math.test.js, import clamp and add tests: values inside the range are returned unchanged, values below return lo, values above return hi, boundaries (x equal to lo or hi) and lo equal to hi work, and assert.throws(() => clamp(5, 10, 0), RangeError).
4. Run `npm test` and make sure it exits 0 with no failing tests. Then open the pull request, mentioning https://github.com/o/r/issues/23.
result.verifier:
Check out the PR head and run each command from the repository root. There is one check per expect line, in order.

Check 1 - expect: "math.js exports clamp(x, lo, hi), which returns x limited to the range lo to hi"
Run:
node -e 'const m=require("./math.js");const c=m.clamp;if(typeof c!=="function"){console.log("FAIL: clamp not exported");process.exit(1)}const cases=[[5,0,10,5],[-5,0,100,0],[140,0,100,100],[0,0,100,0],[100,0,100,100],[3,3,3,3],[-2.5,-10,-1,-2.5],[-20,-10,-1,-10]];let ok=true;for(const [x,lo,hi,want] of cases){const got=c(x,lo,hi);if(got!==want){ok=false;console.log("FAIL clamp("+x+","+lo+","+hi+") = "+got+", want "+want)}}console.log(ok?"PASS":"FAIL");process.exit(ok?0:1)'
PASS: it prints PASS and exits 0 (clamp is an exported function and every case returns x limited to [lo, hi]). FAIL: it prints any FAIL line, throws, or exits non-zero.

Check 2 - expect: "clamp(x, lo, hi) throws a RangeError when lo is greater than hi"
Run:
node -e 'const c=require("./math.js").clamp;if(typeof c!=="function"){console.log("FAIL: clamp not exported");process.exit(1)}let ok=true;for(const [x,lo,hi] of [[5,10,0],[0,1,0],[50,100,-100]]){try{c(x,lo,hi);ok=false;console.log("FAIL clamp("+x+","+lo+","+hi+") did not throw")}catch(e){if(!(e instanceof RangeError)){ok=false;console.log("FAIL clamp("+x+","+lo+","+hi+") threw "+(e&&e.name)+", not RangeError")}}}console.log(ok?"PASS":"FAIL");process.exit(ok?0:1)'
PASS: it prints PASS and exits 0 (every call with lo > hi throws an instance of RangeError). FAIL: any call does not throw, throws something other than a RangeError, or the command exits non-zero.

Check 3 - expect: "README.md documents every function math.js exports"
Run:
node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const names=Object.keys(require("./math.js")).filter(n=>typeof require("./math.js")[n]==="function");const md=fs.readFileSync("README.md","utf8");const missing=names.filter(n=>!md.includes(n+"("));console.log("exported functions: "+names.join(", "));console.log(missing.length?"FAIL not documented in README.md: "+missing.join(", "):"PASS");process.exit(missing.length?1:0)'
Then open README.md and, for each function name the command lists, confirm the README contains a description of what that function does (not just a bare mention).
PASS: the command prints PASS and exits 0, and each listed function (expected at least add, subtract, multiply, clamp) has a description in README.md. FAIL: the command lists any missing function or exits non-zero, or a listed function is only mentioned without saying what it does. Note subtract is missing from README.md at the base commit, so the PR must add it.

Check 4 - expect: "npm test passes"
Run:
npm test; echo "exit $?"
PASS: the last line is 'exit 0' and the TAP summary shows '# fail 0'. FAIL: any non-zero exit or any failing test.

Advisory (not part of PASS/FAIL):
- Whether clamp(5, 5, 5) returns 5 without throwing (lo equal to hi) is covered by case [3,3,3,3] in check 1.
- It is good if test/math.test.js gains tests for clamp, including a RangeError case, and if the README clamp entry mentions the RangeError; neither is required by the expect lines.
- Note in your report whether existing exports add, subtract, multiply still behave as before.
